content: Relacore is a herbal dietary supplement produced by the Carter Reed Company, a brand under Basic Research based in Salt Lake City, Utah. It is marketed with claims that it can help reduce stress and manage cortisol levels. Some companies have previously suggested that elevated cortisol levels are a significant factor contributing to body fat accumulation in women over the age of 30. In October 2004, the United States Federal Trade Commission (FTC) accused the marketers of similar products, CortiSlim and CortiStress, of making false or unsubstantiated claims in their advertisements. Following this, the manufacturers of these products revised their marketing strategies. By January 2006, advertisements for Relacore described it more vaguely as a feel-good pill that purportedly reduces stress, though the exact mechanisms were not specified. The underlying concept is that stress leads to increased cortisol production, and Relacore aims to address this issue. The primary active ingredient associated with cortisol regulation in Relacore is Magnolia bark. The product is also advertised as being free of stimulants. According to marketing claims by Basic Research, Relacore was the best-selling dietary supplement as of June 26, 2006, with reported sales of $23.9 million and 900,000 bottles sold. Supplement Watch notes that honokiol, a compound found in Magnolia bark extract, may help alleviate stress without causing drowsiness when taken in small doses. However, larger doses of honokiol may have sedative effects. When compared to pharmaceutical agents like Valium (diazepam), honokiol appears to exhibit similar anti-anxiety properties but with significantly less sedative potency.
